options.name: Special Events Cost Recovery (expand personnel and non-personnel cost recovery)
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Event organizers and City partners (e.g., parade/festival/stadium/athletic-event sponsors) would bear a greater share of City costs; City recovers previously unreimbursed special-events expenses.
options.feasibility_note: In 2024 the City incurred at least ~$32.3m in direct costs supporting special events but recovered only ~$7.4m. EY estimates the City could have recovered an additional ~$6.3m without changing any ordinances, and a further ~$14.7m with ordinance expansion in line with peer cities (total ~$21m). Headline Exec Summary figure for this workstream is $21m. Components include recovering CPD personnel costs for festivals/athletic/stadium events, recovering the full 150% overtime rate, recovering athletic-event personnel and non-personnel costs, and amending ordinances for CPD/CFD/DSS/CDOT recovery. NOTE: the $11.9m non-city-sponsored parade recovery captured separately is a COMPONENT of this $21m total — avoid double counting.
options.verbatim_anchor: recover an additional ~$6.3m of costs incurred in 2024

options.name: Recover costs for non-city-sponsored parades (amend ordinances)
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Organizers of non-city-sponsored parades, the single largest unrecovered special-events cost category for the City.
options.feasibility_note: Requires amending ordinances to allow cost recovery from parades that are not city-sponsored; peer cities (New York, New Orleans, Los Angeles) have such language. This $11.9m figure is realized only with ordinance change and is a component of the ~$21m special-events workstream total (avoid double counting). Excludes parades protected/officially sponsored.
options.verbatim_anchor: recover up to $11.9m in costs based on a similar approach

options.name: Include Fire/EMS services as recoverable special-events costs
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Special-event organizers; CFD currently incurs significant Fire/EMS costs that are excluded from cost-recovery language.
options.feasibility_note: Fire/EMS services are not broadly included for cost recovery (except athletic events and film permits, neither consistently billed). Option modeled on Dallas, which invoices organizers after the event for all on-duty fire-rescue personnel and vehicles, payment due within 15 business days. No discrete dollar figure stated.
options.verbatim_anchor: Include Fire/EMS services as recoverable costs similar to Dallas

options.name: Establish a tiered special-events fee structure
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Event organizers; fees scaled by expected impact on City services (attendees, density).
options.feasibility_note: Chicago's special-events fees are typically fixed and not scaled by expected impact. Option: establish a tiered fee system like Atlanta and Dallas, based on estimated attendees and stratifying the City into low/medium/high density. Also recommends a consistent permit timeline (30/60/90 days) and a 5-year cadence for fee review/benchmarking. No discrete dollar figure stated.
options.verbatim_anchor: Establish a tiered fee system like Atlanta and Dallas

options.name: Simplify, harmonize, and centralize special-events ordinances and permitting
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: City departments and event organizers; improves cost tracking, transparency, and interdepartmental coordination.
options.feasibility_note: Process reforms: harmonize/simplify ordinance language, centralize ordinances, use a cost calculator with post-event true-up, consider removing 'in excess of 12 shifts' language, move parade/public-assembly permits into the DCASE online portal, generate a unique event ID, build a shared master calendar, and enter intergovernmental agreements with Parks and sister agencies. Monetary benefit not quantified.
options.verbatim_anchor: Harmonize and simplify language among current ordinances

options.name: Establish Fleet Utilization Metrics (utilization targets, right-sizing, pooling)
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Using departments operating the City's 15,000+ asset fleet; reduces excess fleet capacity (City averages 17 vehicles/FTE vs industry 65).
options.feasibility_note: Estimated savings represent 2%-4% of addressable fleet spend from right-sizing, reduced R&M, expanded pooling, reduced future acquisitions. High end depends on ~5 vehicle-coordinator FTEs. Initiatives PM1, PM2, OT5, OS3, OT7. Total fleet workstream savings $16.5m-$30.9m; implementation cost one-time $3.2m-$4.2m plus $1.05m/yr recurring.
options.verbatim_anchor: Establish Fleet Utilization Metrics $2.9 $5.8

options.name: Accelerate Disposition Process (outsource/streamline disposal of inactive vehicles)
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: City fleet (2FM) and Department of Procurement Services; one-time resale proceeds from inactive/long-hold vehicles.
options.feasibility_note: Estimate based on ~700 long-hold vehicles (~33% of long-hold population) plus 1,889 owned vehicles flagged for disposition, multiplied by prior DPS auction sales proceeds (~$1,769 per vehicle). High end reflects increased resale value minus commissions/fees via third-party brokers. Initiative OT1.

options.name: Repair & Maintenance Optimization (MRU analysis, mechanic KPIs, insource/outsource strategy)
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: 2FM maintenance operations and mechanics; affects overtime, outsourcing mix, and preventative maintenance.
options.feasibility_note: 5%-10% estimated saving in R&M spend from reduced overtime, outsourcing costs, labor hours/mechanic productivity, and unplanned maintenance. Year-1 implementation may temporarily increase R&M spend (mechanic hiring, increased PM). Initiatives RM1, RM2, RM3, RM4, OT3.

options.name: Expanded Warranty Recovery

Excludes current warranty recovery of ~$300k/yr. Depends on ~2 additional analyst FTEs. Initiative OS1.

options.name: Improved Acquisition Standard Specifications (exceptions management, standardize specs)

options.name: Office portfolio consolidation (net cost savings from consolidated office space)

options.name: Net revenue from selling vacated office buildings

options.who_is_affected: City (seller) and real-estate buyers; sale of City-owned office buildings vacated through consolidation.
options.feasibility_note: Net sales proceeds (after transaction/closing costs) over 10 years on a present-value basis. Low ($16.3m, Scenario 1) = sell one City-owned building; High ($29.1m, Scenario 2) = sell four City-owned buildings.

options.name: Sale of industrial and other non-office buildings in high-value markets
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: City (seller) and redevelopment buyers; five non-office properties in neighborhoods with strong real-estate markets.
options.feasibility_note: Estimated net sales proceeds (after transaction/closing costs) of ~$57.9m over 10 years on a present-value basis (same in both scenarios). Market comparables suggest land values of $225-$450/sq ft. Proceeding to disposition would require an additional operational/co-location assessment to vacate facilities.
options.verbatim_anchor: Net revenue from sale of additional buildings in high-value markets

options.name: Standardize Riverwalk concession gross-revenue-share fees at 15%
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Riverwalk food-and-beverage concessionaires (established businesses; excludes Community Marketplace vendors).
options.feasibility_note: Incremental revenue ~$13.3m over 10 years on a present-value basis (Table 2 high range shows $13.2m). In 2024 the City earned ~$2.5m in gross-revenue-share fees; peer/benchmark fees range 11%-17%. A flat 15% fee aligns the City with national benchmarks. Most concession agreements expire in 2027; phased/incentive-based implementation recommended.
options.verbatim_anchor: standardizing gross revenue share fees for Riverwalk concessionaires at 15%

options.name: Accelerated sales of large land assemblages (50 assemblages, 165 acres)
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: City (seller) and developers; sale of 50 prioritized, contiguous land assemblages totaling 165 acres from 10,400+ vacant City-owned parcels.
options.feasibility_note: Estimated net sales proceeds (after transaction/closing costs) ~$45.8m over 10 years on a present-value basis. Parcels selected by contiguity, zoning compatibility, and 1-acre minimum size. Recommends a permit-first pilot, developer prequalification, and phasing sales over 10 years to align with market absorption.

options.name: Real estate governance, data, and leasing policy reforms
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: All City departments occupying real estate; centralizes authority and introduces departmental accountability for space usage.
options.feasibility_note: Centralize real-estate authority/budget oversight within 2FM, standardize lease templates and centralize approvals, implement a chargeback methodology, launch a unified real-estate data platform, adopt a citywide workplace strategy, and align real-estate goals with capital planning. Enables the building/land strategies above but is not separately quantified.
options.verbatim_anchor: Centralize real estate-related authority, responsibility and budget oversight

options.name: Adjust top 14 high-impact fees and fines (peer-benchmark / inflation / full cost recovery)

options.feasibility_note: Upper bound on a 'peer maximum' (PM) or inflation (INF) basis. Highest-potential items: >$5m each — vehicle immobilization (boot), towing, storage, driveway permit; $2-$5m — canopy permit, regulated/limited business license, food violation citation, recycling fines. Many municipal-code fees require City Council approval; some have CPI mechanisms capped at 2.5%-5%. Combined FY24 revenue of these 14 was $34.1m.

options.name: Adjust additional fees and fines (Table 2 portfolio)

options.feasibility_note: Incremental revenue subtotal $10.2m-$18.8m, EXCLUDING the Vehicle Sticker Tax (allocated to the Vehicle Fund, captured separately). FY24 revenue (excluding vehicle sticker tax) for this group was $35.6m. Some fees never updated; some indexed to CPI.

options.name: Increase the Vehicle Sticker Tax toward full road-maintenance cost recovery
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Chicago vehicle owners; revenue is allocated to the Vehicle Fund (not the Corporate Fund).
options.feasibility_note: Generated $118.6m-$119m for the Vehicle Fund in FY24 at the current $100 fee, covering ~one-third of road-maintenance expenditure. Increasing the fee from $100 to $259 would provide full recovery of road-maintenance costs; report notes the tax could provide a significant source of revenue (~$207m) for the Vehicle Fund if increased to fully offset costs. Table 2 shows incremental revenue range $0-$187.5m. EXCLUDED from the workstream's $20m-$74m Corporate Fund total because it is allocated to a dedicated fund. Updated every 2 years.
options.verbatim_anchor: increasing the fee from $100 to $259

options.feasibility_note: Mid-term implementation. Estimated annual financial impact is 'Low' (no dollar figure stated). Preserves institutional knowledge and reduces turnover disruption.
options.verbatim_anchor: Centralize succession planning and knowledge transfer efforts within HR

options.name: Transition to performance-based / outcome-based budgeting
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Office of Budget and Management (OBM), all City departments, and residents; aligns budget with Mayoral Investment Pillars (Housing/Homelessness, Mental Health/Wellness, Youth/Economy, Community Safety, Effective Governance).
options.feasibility_note: Savings listed as 'TBD' in the Executive Summary. Structural/governance reform: build service mapping, cost allocation, KPI framework, Results Teams, and Requests for Results; two-phase implementation over ~13 months; may require external investment for the first cycle. No dollar estimate provided.
options.verbatim_anchor: Designing a path toward performance-based budgeting

options.name: CFD: Reduce minimum manning from 5 to 4
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: CFD firefighters (potential reduction of ~456 FTEs, 11% of Fire Suppression & Rescue FTEs) and the CFD collective bargaining unit.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative fiscal impact $517.4m (Year 1 $9.0m; steady-state ~$52m/yr, full savings possibly by Year 8 via ~60 firefighters/yr attrition). Fiscal impact Large, Feasibility LOW. Minimum manning is outlined in the CBA and changes must be negotiated. Requires a standards-of-cover study; may affect ISO rating. Smaller ~$8m/yr savings possible via reassigning to high-overtime units instead of cutting FTEs. NOTE: report headline figures for this workstream are 10-year cumulative totals, not annual.
options.verbatim_anchor: Reduce minimum manning from 5 to 4

options.name: CFD: Convert a portion of ALS ambulances to Basic Life Support (BLS)
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Paramedics (potentially displaced; ~365 paramedics replaced with EMTs) and residents receiving EMS transport.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative net impact $131.1m (Year 1 $11.9m; steady-state ~$14-15m/yr gross, minus ~$1m/yr incremental costs). City operates 80 ambulances (all ALS); 57% of transports were BLS in 2024; could convert 46 ALS to BLS. Fiscal Large, Feasibility Medium. CFD raised triage concerns about dispatching a BLS unit to an ALS-level emergency.
options.verbatim_anchor: Converting advanced life support ambulances to BLS to reduce operating cost

options.name: CFD: Civilianize sworn positions
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: 76 sworn CFD positions (in Inspections and Public Education) recommended for civilianization; affects the bargaining unit for those positions.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative impact $76.8m (Year 1 $3.7m; ~$89k average annual savings per position plus ~$0.4m/yr from duty-availability/uniform pay). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility High. ~60% of recommended positions have budgeted vacancies; full savings may take 1-2 years; results in a change of bargaining unit.
options.verbatim_anchor: Changing sworn positions with civilian responsibilities to civilian positions

options.name: CFD: New fee for false fire alarms
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Commercial and residential property owners triggering false fire alarms; lower-income residents disproportionately unless income-based relief adopted.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative revenue $72.3m (Year 1 $6.6m). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility High, Quick win. Tiered schedule: $500 (1st)/$667 (2nd)/$833 (3rd)/$1,000 (4th offense). May require City Council approval. Waiving the first false-alarm fee would reduce Year-1 impact by ~$1.9m. Seattle offers a grace period via an alarm-user class.
options.verbatim_anchor: Implement a fee for response to false fire alarms

options.name: CFD: New fire alarm inspection, hazmat material, and high-rise inspection fees
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Businesses receiving fire alarm inspections, hazmat material response, and high-rise inspections.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative revenue $61.1m (Year 1 $5.6m). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility High, Quick win. Proposed fees: fire alarm inspection $498/inspection; hazmat response $1,800/response; high-rise inspection $2,292/inspection. May require City Council approval. The City tracks hazmat responses (365 in 2023) and fire alarm inspections (4,123 in 2023).
options.verbatim_anchor: Fire alarm inspection fee, hazmat material fee, and high-rise inspection fee

options.name: CFD: Introduce light-duty positions to expedite returns from lay-ups
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: CFD personnel on lay-up due to duty/non-duty injuries; reduces reliance on costly overtime.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative impact $62.8m (Year 1 $0; savings begin Year 2 ~$6.4m/yr). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility Medium. In 2024 ~$36m overtime cost was incurred due to lay-ups; a 20% reduction yields ~$6.4m annual cost recovery by Year 2. Light-duty positions must be bargained per the CBA; savings may not realize until FY27.
options.verbatim_anchor: Expedite CFD returns from lay-ups to reduce overtime costs

options.name: CFD: Divert 911 calls to hospital-based telehealth
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Residents with non-emergent/chronic-condition 911 calls (~8% of calls) and ~21 EMS personnel; high-need communities gain a telehealth access point.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative net impact $29.4m (Year 1 $2.5m). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility Medium. ~$2m/yr personnel savings (reduce ~21 EMS personnel) plus ~$506k/yr operational savings; ~$200k upfront training. Modeled on Houston's ETHAN program. OEMC must act as connector to hospital partners.
options.verbatim_anchor: Reduce ambulance dispatches and lower paramedic operational costs

options.name: CFD: Increase existing pyrotechnics fee and sprinkler plan-review fee
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Applicants for pyrotechnics permits and sprinkler plan reviews; fees currently below peer cities.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative revenue $17.3m (Year 1 $1.6m). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility High, Quick win. Proposed: pyrotechnics $600 (current $200); sprinkler plan review first 100 sprinklers $731 (current $300), additional heads $5/head (current $1), resubmittal $200. May require City Council approval.
options.verbatim_anchor: Pyrotechnics fee and sprinkler plan review fee

options.name: CFD: EMS cost recovery via a Treat-No-Transport (TNT) fee
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Patients treated on-scene without transport; the City can mitigate equity impacts with flexible collection policies.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative revenue $9.8m (Year 1 $0.9m). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility High, Quick win. TNT is generally not covered by Medicaid/Medicare; federal H.R.2538 (CARE Act of 2025), if approved, could increase revenue potential by $10m annually. Peer cities (Houston, San Diego, NYC) bill $150-$1,000 for TNT.
options.verbatim_anchor: Treat-No-Transport (TNT) fee

options.name: CFD: New fee for non-emergent lift assists at assisted-living facilities / nursing homes
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Assisted-living facilities and nursing homes (567 lift assists there in 2024); waiver/income-based relief possible for facilities serving lower-income populations.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative revenue $3.4m (Year 1 $0.3m; ~$0.3m-$0.4m/yr). Fiscal Small, Feasibility High, Quick win. Illinois HB2336 (awaiting Governor's signature as of June 2025) would allow IL fire departments to charge for non-emergency lift assists. Fees cannot exceed actual personnel/equipment costs; estimate based on Medicare minimum charge (~$550, Bangor ME).
options.verbatim_anchor: Begin charging for Non-Emergent Lift Assists for assisted living facilities

options.name: CPD: Civilianize sworn positions
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: 80 sworn CPD positions found suitable for civilianization (across CompStat, Court Section, Evidence & Recovered Property, HR, Labor Relations, Legal Affairs, Professional Counseling, Training).
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative impact $78.4m (Year 1 $3.7m; ~$93k average savings per position; ~$7m/yr once fully civilianized). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility High. CPD is actively filling 337 newly civilianized positions; contract language and union dynamics may create resistance. 98% of recommended roles have unfilled Patrol Services vacancies.
options.verbatim_anchor: Changing sworn position with civilian responsibilities to civilian positions

options.name: CPD: Disband the Mounted Units Division
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: CPD mounted unit (25 horses, 17 officers, 4 sergeants, 1 lieutenant); officers reassigned to vacant Patrol Services positions.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative net impact $63.9m (Year 1 $5.9m; ~$6m-$7m/yr personnel savings plus ~$115k one-time horse-sale revenue). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility Medium. Peer cities Baltimore, Boston, Seattle, Kansas City, Cincinnati, and Washington D.C. have disbanded mounted units. May impact public perception/morale (horses named after fallen officers).
options.verbatim_anchor: Reducing operating & personnel costs with a one-time revenue increase

options.name: CPD: Implement an Early Warning System (EWS) for problematic officers
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Residents (reduced police misconduct, which disproportionately affects lower-income residents and racial minorities) and the City's settlement/judgment budget.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative net impact $38.8m as COST AVOIDANCE (Year 1 -$1.5m investment; benefit from Year 2). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility High. CPD incurred >$1.11b in verdict/settlement costs 2008-2024; an 11% reduction toward peer average could yield $5m+/yr after a 4-year implementation. CPD has a consent decree requiring an EWS; currently contracting with Benchmark Analytics; implementation delayed to 2026.
options.verbatim_anchor: Reduce incidents by implementing an EWS for problematic police officers

options.name: CPD: New fee for false burglar alarms
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Property owners triggering false burglar alarms (City total burglar alarm count 45,026); lower-income residents disproportionately unless income-based relief adopted.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative revenue $30.7m (Year 1 $2.8m). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility High, Quick win. Schedule: $0 (1st)/$0 (2nd)/$115 (3rd)/$215 (4th offense) — no fee for first two offenses built into estimate. May require City Council approval; could be coupled with a registration fee.
options.verbatim_anchor: False burglar alarm fee

options.name: CPD: Increase first-time DUI fee to national standards
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: First-time DUI offenders; lower-income residents disproportionately unless income-based relief adopted.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative revenue $11.7m (Year 1 $1.1m). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility High, Quick win. Chicago charges $500-$2,500 for first-time DUI; peer cities (NYC, Philadelphia, Columbus, Denver, Seattle) range $1,000-$5,000. May require City Council approval; revenue tracked in FMPS.
options.verbatim_anchor: First time DUI fee

options.name: CPD: Use autonomous drones to replace one helicopter unit
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: CPD aerial unit (operates 4 helicopters, 5 existing drones); residents (privacy concerns).
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative net impact $6.0m (Year 1 $0.5m). Fiscal Small, Feasibility Medium. 6 new drones (~$0.1m one-time) could replace the Bell 206 helicopter; 10-year savings driven by $1.3m fuel, $1.9m maintenance, $2.4m personnel, plus a one-time ~$1.5m helicopter sale (subject to federal grant claw-back exemption). IL state law (ILCS 167 / Drone Surveillance Act) restricts general surveillance.
options.verbatim_anchor: Replacing one helicopter unit with drones to improve cost efficiency

options.name: CPD: Increase film-production squad-car usage fee
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Film productions using squad cars for traffic control; fee currently below peer cities.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative revenue $2.0m (Year 1 $0.2m). Fiscal Small, Feasibility High, Quick win. Chicago charges $150/squad car/day; peer cities (Minneapolis, Columbus) range $160-$200/day. May require City Council approval.
options.verbatim_anchor: Film production fee – Squad car usage

options.name: OEMC: Replace CPD traffic overtime with full-time traffic management + parking enforcement roles
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Traffic Management Authority (TMA) staff and parking-enforcement workforce (SEIU Local 73); CPD relieved of ~$17m/yr overtime for TMA vacancies.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative net impact $84.2m (Year 1 $4.3m) — ~$81.7m additional parking-enforcement revenue plus ~$2.5m operational savings. Fiscal Medium, Feasibility Medium. Hire 169 full-time hybrid roles (50/50 TMA/parking enforcement). 2024 parking-enforcement collected ~$65m; fines assessed $125m. Assumes gradual ramp (50%/80%/100% of roles filled in Years 1-3) and a 10% salary increase for parking-enforcement roles. Requires SEIU Local 73 discussions.
options.verbatim_anchor: Replacing CPD overtime hours for traffic with new full-time traffic mgmt

options.name: OEMC: Reduce 311 call center hours and add chatbot automation
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: 311 call-center operators/supervisors (high employee displacement) and residents (high-utilizers and older demographics preferring phone calls).
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative total impact $40.1m (Year 1 $2.0m; cost savings $32.8m plus $13.1m incremental chatbot savings, net of investment $5.9m). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility High, Quick win. 311 currently operates 24/7 (2.3m calls in 2024); transition to a reduced 12-hour schedule like LA/Philadelphia. ~$33m over 10 years from reduced hours; ~$13m more via chatbot. 16 operator positions are Airport-fund-funded.
options.verbatim_anchor: Reduce hours of operation and services offered via 311 call center

options.name: OEMC: Institute a pool of retired 911 dispatchers to reduce FMLA-driven overtime
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: 911 call-center staff (Police/Fire operators and supervisors); part-time pool could be retired City/County dispatchers (IBEW Local 21/9).
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative net impact $31.0m (Year 1 -<$0.1m; ~$3.4m-$4.0m/yr from Year 2). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility Medium. In 2024 OEMC used 59,309 FMLA hours (~90% at the 911 call center); overtime was >15% of hours worked and $10.4m (21%) of wages. ~170 part-time employees (~1,000 hrs/yr each) needed to fully offset overtime; part-time dispatchers require no fringe benefits. ~$40k/yr EAP investment.
options.verbatim_anchor: Institute a pool of retired 911 dispatchers to reduce overtime costs

options.name: OPSA: Install cameras in CFD vehicles and utilize existing CPD cameras
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: CFD and CPD drivers; unions in Atlanta and Baltimore criticized camera installation as punishing employees for minor infractions.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative net impact $28.8m (Year 1 -$0.5m; ramps up over 2 years). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility Medium. CFD/CPD incurred $1.4m/$3.8m in vehicular repair costs in 2024; Baltimore saw a 70% decrease in accident-related repair costs. CFD could install cameras in ~250 vehicles at $2,000 each (~$500k upfront) plus $50k/yr storage; adds 4 civilian Digital Intelligence Analyst FTEs at $137k each.
options.verbatim_anchor: Install cameras to increase accountability, reduce vehicle abuse, and mitigate accidents

options.name: OPSA: Eliminate vacant timekeeper roles via new ERP payroll solution
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: Vacant timekeeper positions (AFSCME Council 31); OPSA budgets 59 timekeeper roles, 30 currently vacant.
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative net impact $25.1m (Year 1 $0; ~$3m/yr from Year 2 once fully implemented). Fiscal Medium, Feasibility High. Eliminating 4 Clerk IV-Payroll and 26 CPD timekeeper budgeted vacancies. ERP payroll implementation expected to take 12 months, completed by start of FY27; ERP cost incurred regardless of this option. Eliminating all 59 roles could save ~$6m/yr. Layoffs of filled positions require seniority-basis bargaining.
options.verbatim_anchor: Implementation of new ERP payroll solution to eliminate need for vacant timekeeper positions

options.name: OPSA: Rent the Public Safety Training Center (PSTC) to state and other municipal departments
options.report: EY Financial and Strategic Reform Options — ey-reform-options.pdf
options.who_is_affected: External public-safety agencies renting PSTC facilities (burn tower, driving pad, outdoor village, virtual simulation, railroad prop, auto extrication, hazmat area, seminars).
options.feasibility_note: 10-year cumulative net impact $3.6m (Year 1 -$0.3m; ~$1.5m/yr gross revenue minus instructor/coordinator/security costs ~$1.0-1.2m/yr). Fiscal Small, Feasibility Medium. Rental fees are preliminary estimates; a cost analysis and business plan are recommended. Could also rent shooting ranges, outdoor areas, and classroom spaces in idle time.
options.verbatim_anchor: Opportunity to generate revenue by renting the training facility

notes: IMPORTANT — UNIT INCONSISTENCY ACROSS WORKSTREAMS: Workstreams 1-7 (Special Events, Fleet, Real Estate except one-time sales, Fees/Fines, Employee Benefits, Procurement, Organizational Analysis) report ANNUAL (recurring) or 10-year-PV figures. Workstream 9 (Service Optimization) reports 10-YEAR CUMULATIVE fiscal-impact totals in its summary tables (p72-74); I captured those 10-year totals as dollar_estimate (unit 'USD') and put Year 1 and steady-state annual figures in feasibility_note. The parent must reconcile these before summing — do NOT add Service Optimization 10-year totals to other workstreams' annual figures. Real Estate figures are 10-year present values discounted at 5% (unit 'USD'). RANGED/AMBIGUOUS FIGURES: (1) Special Events workstream total is ~$21m = ~$6.3m recoverable without ordinance change + ~$14.7m with ordinance change; the $11.9m parade recovery is a COMPONENT of this total (captured as a separate row with a double-count warning). (2) Fleet p15 narrative text lists warranty recovery at '$2.2m-$4.4m' but the authoritative tables (p16/p19/p20) list Expanded Warranty Recovery at $1.7m-$3.7m and Lifecycle/Replacement Strategy at $2.2m-$4.4m — I used the table figures. (3) Fees & Fines workstream Corporate-Fund total is $20m-$74m EXCLUDING the Vehicle Sticker Tax (allocated to the dedicated Vehicle Fund); the vehicle sticker is captured separately with range $0-$187.5m (Table 2) and a full-cost-recovery figure of ~$207m / fee increase $100→$259. (4) Procurement per-category savings percentages and dollars are REDACTED in the source; only the $55m-$111m total is available. (5) Performance-Based Budgeting savings are 'TBD' (null). (6) Org Analysis option #11 (succession planning) impact is 'Low' (null); option #4 (streamline position management) $25m is potential REVENUE not cost savings. (7) Several benefits options (LOA continuation, COBRA communications) have $0M potential savings as stated. WORKSTREAM EXEC-SUMMARY TOTALS (low-high, $M): Special Events $21; Fleet $17-$31; Real Estate $157-$202; Fees/Fines $20-$74; Employee Benefits $80-$103; Procurement $55-$111; Organizational $148-$257; Performance Budgeting TBD; Service Optimization $33-$597; GRAND TOTAL $530-$1,396. has_dissent is FALSE for every entry — EY is a consultant analysis with no formal recorded dissents; union opposition/CBA-negotiation constraints noted in feasibility_note where stated (e.g., minimum manning, civilianization, fleet cameras, timekeeper roles).
